messages:
maria: Drafting a short 'fast path' CVE + dependency patch prioritization playbook. Putting a compact version here for quick consumption — want signoff on SLAs and ownership mappings. Link to full doc: https://internal.redwood/sec/fast-path (WIP)

anil: +1. Can we include a KMS-dep note? some KMS client CVEs need coord with infra for key rotation windows.

maria: yes — add a KMS annex. For KMS CVEs: treat as P0 if they can leak KEKs or allow key import. Otherwise P1.

liz: propose we call it Fast-Path: when an exploit exists or PoC published -> immediate unblock path. Otherwise standard triage.

maria: agreed. Here's the proposed triage matrix (condensed):
```
Severity -> Criteria -> Ack SLA -> Patch SLA -> Rollout SLA
P0 -> RCE / auth bypass / KMS key compromise -> ack <1h -> patch+canary <72h -> full rollback-capable rollout <24h after canary
P1 -> priv-esc / sustained DoS / data exposure w/o keys -> ack <6h -> patch <7d -> staged rollouts over 48-72h
P2 -> info/low-impact deps -> ack <72h -> schedule in next sprint -> normal rollout cadence
```

maria: Ownership mapping: security (triage lead, coordinates severity), component owner (implements patch), infra (deploy/canary/rollout), oncall-sre (emergency rollback/runbook).

security-bot: Automated CVE alerts: 2026-03-18: pkg/crypto 1.2.3 -> RCE PoC reported. Affects runtime and worker pools.

anil: That alert is real — runtime uses a vendored submodule. Action: anil to open GH issue and draft PR, maria to assign severity and ping infra.

maria: I'm taking severity. Marking as P0. Notifying infra for canary window. @anil please include KMS client impact analysis in PR description.

anil: Will do. ETA for PR: 18h.

liz: For rollout, let's use canary group = 5% of capacity for 2 hours with perf/err gates. If everything looks green, ramp to 50% over next 4 hours then 100% if no regressions. Include automatic fallback to previous image.

oncall-sre: Add these commands to the runbook for rollback and log collection:
```bash
# rollback to previous deployment
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service runtime --to=previous
# collect pod logs for last 30m
kubectl logs -l app=runtime --since=30m > /tmp/runtime-logs.txt
```

oncall-sre: Also add a short checklist: notify customers (if hit SLA), open incident ticket, page oncall, escalate to execs if >4h outage.

maria: Good checklist. Two quick questions: 1) who owns the initial customer-facing message? 2) do we want an exec escalation threshold lower than 4h for KMS-related incidents?

liz: Security comms should draft initial message, product comms approves. Exec threshold: for KMS P0 (key compromise) we should page L3 and execs immediately.

anil: Suggest we encode the escalation ladder as tags in the GH issue: severity:P0, escalation:exec,KMS if needed. That makes automation easier.

maria: I'll update the doc with those tags and the KMS annex. Final ask: everyone react with :thumbsup: if they approve the condensed playbook here so I can promote to the canonical runbook.

liz: :thumbsup:

anil: :thumbsup:

oncall-sre: :thumbsup: (added rollback commands to the runbook PR)

security-bot: Note: added automation to create issue templates for P0/P1 with required fields: impact, exploit-evidence, affected services, component-owner, canary-plan.

maria: Excellent — thank you. I'll spin up the formal runbook PR this afternoon and tag owners. If anything changes after the PR lands, re-open this thread.

liz: Thanks all. Short and clear — exactly what we need for rapid response. :white_check_mark:
